- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5) and forecast is significantly above recent history, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent high, apply a 1–2 day lag correction: subtract 1–2% from next 2–3 periods to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5) and forecast is below recent history, increase forecast by 5–10% to counteract pessimism.  
- If true outcome consistently deviates from forecast by >3% over 3–5 periods, apply mean reversion: adjust forecast toward recent 5-day average.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above 18-day history, reduce by 10–15% unless sentiment is strong bullish (≥ 0.7).  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.4) and forecast is >10% above or below history, apply a 2–3 period smoothing filter to dampen volatility.
